summary: The eShop Modernizing repository contains a parallel ASP.NET MVC5/WebAPI2 legacy application (src/eShopLegacyMVC) and an ASP.NET Core 2.2 ported application (eShopPorted), both implementing a product catalog CRUD system with shared utility classes. Key business rules extracted include mandatory name/price fields, price range restrictions (0–1,000,000), stock management thresholds, pagination logic, identifier generation via HiLo sequences (legacy only), picture URI construction, and mock/real service selection via configuration flags. Two primary user journeys are identified: catalog browsing with pagination and catalog item CRUD operations. The extraction is constrained by incomplete evidence on some business conditions (e.g., reorder logic triggers, validation error handling specifics) and duplicate/divergent implementations across the two codebases.

rules.title: Catalog Item Price Validation
rules.description: CatalogItem.Price must be a positive decimal with maximum two decimal places and must fall within the range [0, 1,000,000]. A RegularExpression validation attribute enforces the format constraint.
conditions: CatalogItem.Price property is being set or updated
Price value is submitted through Create or Edit form
outcomes: Price is validated against the regex pattern ^\d+(\.\d{0,2})*$
If validation fails, error message returned: 'The field Price must be a positive number with maximum two decimals.'
If validation passes, price is persisted to the database

evidence.observation: CatalogItem.Price decorated with [RegularExpression(@"^\d+(\.\d{0,2})*$", ErrorMessage = "The field Price must be a positive number with maximum two decimals.")] and [Range(0, 1000000)]
Identical Price validation constraints present in legacy model

rules.title: Stock Availability Range Constraint
rules.description: CatalogItem.AvailableStock must be a non-negative integer in the range [0, 10,000,000]. A Range attribute enforces this constraint.
conditions: AvailableStock property is set during Create or Edit
outcomes: If AvailableStock < 0 or > 10,000,000, validation error returned: 'The field Stock must be between 0 and 10 million.'
If valid, AvailableStock is persisted

evidence.observation: [Range(0, 10000000, ErrorMessage = "The field Stock must be between 0 and 10 million.")] applied to AvailableStock property
Identical constraint in legacy codebase

rules.title: Restock Threshold Range Validation
rules.description: CatalogItem.RestockThreshold must be a non-negative integer between 0 and 10,000,000, enforced by a Range attribute.
conditions: RestockThreshold is being modified
outcomes: If RestockThreshold outside [0, 10000000], error 'The field Restock must be between 0 and 10 million.' is raised
If valid, RestockThreshold is saved

evidence.observation: [Range(0, 10000000, ErrorMessage = "The field Restock must be between 0 and 10 million.")] on RestockThreshold

rules.title: Max Stock Threshold Limit
rules.description: CatalogItem.MaxStockThreshold must be a non-negative integer between 0 and 10,000,000 due to physical/logistical warehouse constraints.
conditions: MaxStockThreshold property is modified
outcomes: If outside [0, 10000000], error raised: 'The field Max stock must be between 0 and 10 million.'
If valid, constraint is satisfied and value persisted

evidence.observation: [Range(0, 10000000, ErrorMessage = "The field Max stock must be between 0 and 10 million.")] on MaxStockThreshold property
Identical constraint in legacy implementation

rules.title: Catalog Item Name Required Field
rules.description: CatalogItem.Name is mandatory and must not be null or empty. Maximum length is 50 characters.
conditions: CatalogItem.Name is null, empty, or exceeds 50 characters
outcomes: Validation fails and name is required to proceed with Create/Edit
Error message indicates name is required

evidence.observation: [Required] and [MaxLength(50)] attributes on Name property
Same constraints in legacy codebase

rules.title: Picture File Name Required
rules.description: CatalogItem.PictureFileName is required and must have a value. Default value is 'dummy.png' if not explicitly set during construction.
conditions: CatalogItem is created or updated without PictureFileName
outcomes: If no PictureFileName provided, default 'dummy.png' is assigned in constructor
PictureFileName is required for database persistence

evidence.observation: Constructor sets PictureFileName = DefaultPictureName ('dummy.png') if not provided; [Required] attribute enforces persistence
Identical behavior in legacy model

rules.title: Pagination of Catalog Items
rules.description: Catalog items are retrieved in paginated batches. Each page is defined by pageSize and pageIndex parameters. Total item count is calculated for pagination UI.
conditions: User requests Catalog/Index endpoint with pageSize and pageIndex query parameters (defaults: pageSize=10, pageIndex=0)
outcomes: Service retrieves total count of all CatalogItems
Service skips (pageSize × pageIndex) items and takes pageSize items from database
PaginatedItemsViewModel is populated with ActualPage, ItemsPerPage, TotalItems, TotalPages, and Data (item collection)
View renders pagination controls based on TotalPages and ActualPage

evidence.observation: Index(int pageSize = 10, int pageIndex = 0) calls service.GetCatalogItemsPaginated(pageSize, pageIndex)
GetCatalogItemsPaginated calculates totalItems, skips and takes based on pageSize/pageIndex, returns PaginatedItemsViewModel with TotalPages = (int)Math.Ceiling(((decimal)count / pageSize))
TotalPages computed as (int)Math.Ceiling(((decimal)count / pageSize)) in constructor

rules.title: Picture URI Construction
rules.description: Picture URI for a catalog item is dynamically constructed as '/Pics/{itemId}.png' in the ported app. In the legacy app, it uses a route helper to construct an absolute URL via the PicController route.
conditions: CatalogItem is retrieved and displayed in a view
outcomes: Ported app: PictureUri is set to '/Pics/{item.Id}.png'
Legacy app: PictureUri is set via Url.RouteUrl(PicController.GetPicRouteName, ...) producing an absolute URL to the PicController.Index route with catalogItemId parameter

evidence.observation: AddUriPlaceHolder method sets item.PictureUri = $"/Pics/{item.Id}.png"
AddUriPlaceHolder method sets item.PictureUri = this.Url.RouteUrl(PicController.GetPicRouteName, new { catalogItemId = item.Id }, this.Request.Url.Scheme)

rules.title: Service Implementation Selection (Mock vs Real)
rules.description: The application can switch between a real database-backed CatalogService and a mock in-memory CatalogServiceMock based on configuration. The eShopPorted appsettings.json exposes a 'UseMockData' flag; logic for conditional registration is inferred but not fully evidenced.
conditions: Application starts
DI container is configured (Autofac)
outcomes: If UseMockData = true, CatalogServiceMock is registered as ICatalogService implementation
If UseMockData = false, real CatalogService is registered
All controller dependencies receive the selected implementation

evidence.observation: Contains "UseMockData": "true" flag
Provides hardcoded in-memory implementation of ICatalogService using PreconfiguredData
Real implementation backed by CatalogDBContext

rules.title: Legacy HiLo Sequence-Based ID Generation
rules.description: In the legacy application, CatalogItem IDs are generated using a custom HiLo (High-Low) sequence pattern. When creating a new CatalogItem, CatalogItemHiLoGenerator.GetNextSequenceValue is called to fetch the next ID from the 'catalog_hilo' SQL sequence.
conditions: CreateCatalogItem is called in legacy CatalogService
ID has not been manually set
outcomes: HiLoGenerator.GetNextSequenceValue executes: 'SELECT NEXT VALUE FOR catalog_hilo;'
Database SQL sequence returns the next ID
ID is assigned to the new CatalogItem before insertion
Item is persisted with the generated ID

evidence.observation: CreateCatalogItem calls catalogItem.Id = indexGenerator.GetNextSequenceValue(db)
GetNextSequenceValue executes db.Database.SqlQuery<Int64>("SELECT NEXT VALUE FOR catalog_hilo;")

rules.title: Catalog Item CRUD Operations
rules.description: The catalog system supports Create, Read, Update, Delete (CRUD) operations on CatalogItem entities. Each operation is exposed through both MVC controller actions and (in legacy) Web API endpoints.
conditions: User navigates to or submits catalog forms (Create, Edit, Delete)
User calls REST API endpoints
outcomes: Create: New CatalogItem is instantiated, validated, persisted via service.CreateCatalogItem()
Read: CatalogItem is retrieved via service.FindCatalogItem(id) or service.GetCatalogItemsPaginated()
Update: Modified CatalogItem is saved via service.UpdateCatalogItem() with EntityState.Modified
Delete: CatalogItem is removed via service.RemoveCatalogItem()

evidence.observation: Index, Details, Create (GET/POST), Edit (GET/POST), Delete (GET/POST), DeleteConfirmed all map to corresponding service methods
Interface defines FindCatalogItem, GetCatalogItemsPaginated, CreateCatalogItem, UpdateCatalogItem, RemoveCatalogItem

rules.title: Image MIME Type Resolution
rules.description: When serving catalog item picture files, the system determines the MIME type based on the file extension (.png, .gif, .jpg, .jpeg, .bmp, .tiff, .wmf, .jp2, .svg). If extension is unrecognized, default 'application/octet-stream' is used.
conditions: PicController.Index is called with a catalogItemId
Item has a PictureFileName with an extension
outcomes: File extension is extracted from PictureFileName
GetImageMimeTypeFromImageFileExtension maps extension to MIME type
File is read from disk and returned with correct Content-Type header

evidence.observation: GetImageMimeTypeFromImageFileExtension switches on imageFileExtension to map .png→image/png, .jpg→image/jpeg, etc.; defaults to application/octet-stream
Identical MIME type resolution logic in legacy implementation

rules.title: Catalog Brand and Type Reference Data
rules.description: The system maintains a fixed set of catalog brands (Azure, .NET, Visual Studio, SQL Server, Other) and catalog types (Mug, T-Shirt, Sheet, USB Memory Stick) as reference data. These are seeded into the database at initialization.
conditions: Database is initialized or migrated
outcomes: 5 CatalogBrand records are inserted with IDs 1–5
4 CatalogType records are inserted with IDs 1–4
Reference data is available for dropdown/selection in Create/Edit forms

evidence.observation: GetPreconfiguredCatalogBrands returns 5 hardcoded brands; GetPreconfiguredCatalogTypes returns 4 hardcoded types
HasData() seeding in Fluent API applies PreconfiguredData.GetPreconfiguredCatalogBrands()
Identical seed data in legacy codebase

rules.title: Anti-Forgery Token Validation on Mutation Endpoints
rules.description: All HTTP POST endpoints that mutate state (Create, Edit, DeleteConfirmed) require an anti-forgery token validated by the [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] attribute to prevent CSRF attacks.
conditions: User submits a form via POST to Create, Edit, or DeleteConfirmed endpoint
Request lacks or has invalid anti-forgery token
outcomes: If token is missing or invalid, request is rejected with HTTP 400 Bad Request
If token is valid, form processing continues

evidence.observation: [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] decorates Create(POST), Edit(POST), and DeleteConfirmed(POST) methods
Same CSRF protection in legacy controller

rules.title: REST API Brand Data Serialization
rules.description: Web API endpoints serving brand data serialize CatalogBrand objects using binary serialization (via eShopLegacy.Utilities.Serializing) for file download responses.
conditions: FilesController.Index or WebApi/FilesController.Get is called
outcomes: Service retrieves CatalogBrand list
Brands are mapped to BrandDTO objects (Id, Brand properties)
DTOs are serialized to binary stream via Serializing.SerializeBinary()
Response is returned as a StreamContent with the serialized bytes

evidence.observation: Index() maps brands to BrandDTO list, calls Serializing().SerializeBinary(brands), returns Ok(data)
Get() similarly serializes brands using Serializing.SerializeBinary() and wraps in HttpResponseMessage with StreamContent

user_journeys.title: Browse Catalog with Pagination
user_journeys.trigger: User navigates to /Catalog/Index or clicks 'Next'/'Previous' pagination link
preconditions: Application is running and database is initialized with seed data
User is viewing a web browser

steps.actor_action: User opens /Catalog/Index in browser (or clicks pagination link with pageSize=10, pageIndex=0)

steps.system_response: Service.GetCatalogItemsPaginated(10, 0) is called, fetches total item count and first 10 items from database
PaginatedItemsViewModel is populated: ActualPage=0, ItemsPerPage=10, TotalItems=N, TotalPages=ceil(N/10), Data=[items 1-10]
For each item, PictureUri is set to /Pics/{item.Id}.png

steps.actor_action: System returns view with pagination controls
steps.system_response: View renders CatalogTable partial with 10 items and pagination UI showing Previous (disabled), page info, Next (enabled if more pages)

alternate_paths: If user navigates to /Catalog/Index?pageSize=5&pageIndex=2, the same flow repeats with pageSize=5, pageIndex=2
user_journeys.outcome: User sees a paginated list of 10 (or custom pageSize) catalog items with clickable pagination controls to browse through pages

user_journeys.title: Create New Catalog Item
preconditions: Admin has access to the application
Database is initialized with brand and type seed data

steps.system_response: CatalogController.Create() (GET) is invoked, populates ViewBag.CatalogBrandId and ViewBag.CatalogTypeId dropdowns from service.GetCatalogBrands/Types()

steps.actor_action: Browser renders /Catalog/Create form with empty fields and anti-forgery token
steps.system_response: User sees form with Name, Description, Brand dropdown, Type dropdown, Price, Picture, Stock, Restock, Max Stock fields

steps.actor_action: Admin fills form: Name='Test Product', Price=19.99, Stock=50, Brand=2 (.NET), Type=2 (T-Shirt), submits POST
System validates all fields (Name required, Price format/range, Stock range, etc.)
steps.system_response: If any validation fails, form is re-rendered with error messages. If all valid, service.CreateCatalogItem(catalogItem) is called.

steps.actor_action: Service persists new item (legacy: generates ID via HiLo, ported: EF Core auto-identity)
steps.system_response: Item inserted into database with generated ID

alternate_paths: If validation fails, form is re-rendered with errors and user must correct and resubmit
user_journeys.outcome: New catalog item is created and persisted; user is redirected to /Catalog/Index to see the updated list
